Japanese blind merch: random, BOX and complete-set labels

By Kokeniwa · Published 2026-10-21 · Sources checked 2026-10-21

A quantity equal to the number of designs does not itself guarantee a complete set. “BOX” also needs an explicit contents statement. Read whether the exact product listing promises all designs, allows duplicates, or sells individual random items.

On this pageSeparate format from the contents promiseWorked example: singles are not the same as the BOXChoose the purchase format for your actual goalDo not invent odds from the design countBefore checkout

Separate format from the contents promise

Japanese labelWhat it tells you—and what to check
ランダムRandom selection; check whether choosing a design is possible
トレーディングA trading product format; read the selection and assortment details
全5種Five designs in the range; not automatically five items in your order
単品 / バラAn individual unit; check its selection rule
BOXA boxed sales unit; check the number and assortment inside
コンプリート / 全種セットA complete-set claim; check which designs it explicitly includes

Worked example: singles are not the same as the BOX

Good Smile’s K-ON! Fuwame trading plush strap listing distinguishes a five-design BOX from individual random purchases. It explicitly says one BOX completes the range, while purchasing five individual units is not supplied as the BOX. In this particular listing, the complete-set promise belongs to the specified BOX product.

Use that example to read other listings, not as a rule for every Good Smile product or every brand. The page was checked on October 21, 2026; its displayed preorder period was earlier in 2026. It is an explanation of wording, not a current stock recommendation.

Sources: Good Smile: K-ON! trading plush strap BOX listing

Choose the purchase format for your actual goal

Your goalEvidence you need
One specific characterA selectable-design listing or a clearly identified individual item
Any surprise from the rangeThe random unit’s quantity and possible contents
Every regular designAn explicit complete-assortment promise for the exact set or BOX
A secret or bonus design tooA statement that it is included; the regular-set promise may not cover it

Do not invent odds from the design count

“Five designs” does not prove equal probabilities, independent draws or a particular carton arrangement. Without those conditions, a probability calculator would create false precision. Even when a seller promises a complete BOX, it does not follow that five loose units have that property.

If duplicates would leave you disappointed, decide the acceptable purchase format before choosing a quantity. Read resale or second-hand listings separately: an opened assortment, an empty BOX and a manufacturer-sealed BOX are materially different offers.

Before checkout

  • Confirm whether your selected variant is a single unit or a BOX.
  • Check items per order, designs in the range and any explicit assortment promise separately.
  • Check whether extras shown in the photo are included in this sales unit.
  • Save the product description and order confirmation so you can identify exactly what you purchased.
  • If the assortment statement is unclear, ask the seller before ordering rather than interpreting the range count as a guarantee.

Sources & scope

  • Good Smile: K-ON! trading plush strap BOX listing

Official sources were checked on 2026-10-21. Translations and calculations are our explanations. Examples are not hands-on product tests, current stock checks or a substitute for the exact seller or event conditions.
